items.description: A Postgres connection string with an inline password sits in an instruction file that attaches to every Copilot request. The credential is live-shaped, not a marked placeholder. The finding must cite location and credential shape only — a report reproducing the value re-leaks it onto a surface that outlives the fix.

CLAUDE.md instructs agents to commit with `git commit --no-verify` whenever pre-commit checks are slow. This is an instruction to use the bypass, not a warning against it, and it defeats every check the hook enforces.

CLAUDE.md tells agents to add `-k` to curl to skip TLS certificate verification when a proxy interferes. Disabling certificate verification as a documented workaround is a standing instruction to accept any certificate.

CLAUDE.md asserts a pre-commit hook blocks any commit containing a credential, and tells readers they need not check by hand. No hook exists anywhere in the repo — no .husky/, no .githooks/, no hook config in package.json. The claim is worse than silence: it stops readers verifying what they believe a mechanism guarantees, and the same file's Copilot sibling already carries a leaked credential.
The bootstrap step pipes a downloaded script straight into a shell (`curl -sL ... | sh`) as a required provisioning step, with no checksum or review between fetch and execution.

No surface documents how to build, test, or lint, while the repo plainly has all three: Makefile targets build/test/lint/fmt and package.json scripts build/test/lint. The evidence must name where the commands exist and that a search of both surfaces found no mention.

"Formatting is enforced automatically on save" names no mechanism the repo carries — prettier is a devDependency and a Makefile fmt target, neither of which runs on save. Either the rule belongs in a formatter config the tooling actually runs, or the enforcement claim goes.
